decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'
I chose Node.js with Express and Mongoose for the sample service.
reason: The user requested a Node.js Mongoose service; Node + Mongoose is the natural fit and matches the prompt.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: 'Builder will treat this as a single-agent code generation task producing a standalone Node.js service with REST endpoints.'

decision: I chose Mongoose 7.x (latest 7.x) and the matching mongodb driver that Mongoose depends on.
reason: Mongoose 7.x is current, compatible with Node 24, and simplifies schema + ref modeling required by the sample.
evidence: Assumption_from_prompt_review: 'Builder will pick a modern Mongoose version compatible with Node.js 24 (e.g., Mongoose 7.x) and the MongoDB Node driver matching Mongoose's peer dependency (mongodb 5.x).'

decision: I chose to read the full connection string from the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime and use it as provided (do not embed credentials in repo).
alternatives: Read full connection string from environment and trust its auth mechanism
reason: The sample must not contain secrets and the environment-provided URI may already encode the recommended auth mechanism; using it keeps the sample simple and secure.
evidence: Run environment: 'Its connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time.'

decision: I chose not to provision any Azure resources and to use the existing cluster from DOCUMENTDB_URI.
alternatives: Provision a new DocumentDB cluster as part of sample
Use the existing cluster pointed to by DOCUMENTDB_URI and do not provision
reason: Provisioning is disallowed by policy; a live reachable cluster is provided for verification.
evidence: Run policy and run-environment: 'Azure resource changes allowed: False.' and 'A DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable.'

decision: I chose to create a separate 'households' collection with documents that reference members (array of ObjectId refs to customers).
alternatives: Embed household members within Customer documents
Store separate Household documents with member refs (ObjectId)
reason: A separate Household collection makes household-level aggregates (CLV, products) straightforward and avoids expanding customer documents; it's a clearer model for this demo.
evidence:
Assumption_from_prompt_review: 'Customer documents include ...; Household documents contain an array of ObjectId refs to customers (Mongoose ref).'
Also documentdb-data-modeling skill guidance that references embedding vs referencing for many-to-many/read patterns.

decision: I chose to create a compound index on { normalizedAddress:1, phone:1, surname:1 } using the documentdb MCP server create_index API, and also declare the index in the Mongoose schema for parity.
alternatives: Create only Mongoose indexes via schema.ensureIndexes
Use documentdb MCP server to create and verify indexes
Do nothing about indexes for the demo
reason: Using MCP server lets us verify index creation and inspect explain plans in the live cluster; declaring in Mongoose ensures the schema is explicit and local dev parity.
evidence: Readiness_report: 'the documentdb MCP server is available for live verification' and assumptions about creating a compound index to support grouping/matching.

decision: I chose @faker-js/faker for synthetic data generation.
reason: Avoid module-not-found and use a maintained faker library compatible with Node 24.
evidence: The seed script needs a maintained faker library; the older 'faker' package may not have a valid main entry. @faker-js/faker is actively maintained.

decision: I chose to create the compound index via Mongoose's schema.ensureIndexes programmatically because the documentdb_create_index MCP call failed.
reason: MCP API failed in this environment; using Mongoose to create the index achieves the same outcome for the sample without provisioning changes.
evidence: Attempted functions.documentdb_create_index returned 'Error: Function failed.' when creating index on customers collection.

decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'

reason: The prompt explicitly requests Node.js and Mongoose.

decision: I chose a compound index on { normalizedAddress:1, phone:1, surname:1 } plus a numeric index on clv and a multikey index on products to support product aggregation.
alternatives: Compound index on normalizedAddress, phone, surname
Separate single-field indexes on address, phone, surname
reason: Compound index follows ESR guidance and will help the grouping queries used in sample; additional clv and products indexes optimize aggregates.
evidence: Assumptions from prompt review: 'Create aggregation pipelines that group on normalized address/phone/surname. Add a compound index on { normalizedAddress:1, phone:1, surname:1 }'.

decision: I chose to use the documentdb MCP server tools to verify collections and sample documents in the live cluster.
alternatives: Verify data using only local scripts (mongoose)
Use documentdb MCP server for data-plane verification (list collections, sample docs)
reason: Provides authoritative, service-oriented verification (index listing, explain) beyond the application-level checks.
